title: Safety fallback automation contract and ChatOps runbook (working draft)
summary: Working draft for an automation-first fallback contract tied to ChatOps controls. Defines signals, escalation boundaries, and example runbook commands for safely reverting or degrading LL M-powered features during canary and A/B experiments.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic automation contract for safety fallbacks during staged rollouts (canaries, microreleases, A/B experiments). The emphasis is: 1) define measurable signals, 2) attach deterministic automation actions, 3) surface human-in-the-loop controls via ChatOps, and 4) provide clear post-mortem telemetry slices. Intended audience: product owners, release stewards, SREs, and experiment stewards.

High-level goals:
- Reduce mean-time-to-safepoint when behavioral or performance regressions are detected.
- Favor automated containment (traffic shift, model swap, degraded feature mode) when safe-to-automate.
- Ensure humans can override automation quickly and predictably via ChatOps.
- Make fallbacks auditable and reversible with clear owner and signal mapping.

Signal taxonomy (priority order):
1) Safety-critical behavioral signals (highest priority)
   - User-safety classifier rate exceedance (e.g., policy-violation rate > 0.2% over 3m rolling window)
   - Hallucination failures with ground-truth connectors (precision drop > 15% vs baseline)
2) Business-impact signals
   - Conversion or billing-impact drop (relative drop > 8% in a cohort within 10m)
   - Revenue-impacting errors (failed checkout routing due to model responses)
3) Performance signals
   - p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline over 5m and sustained for 3 datapoints
   - Token-error spikes / malformed responses > threshold
4) Infrastructure signals
   - GPU OOM/worker crash rate > 5% in 10m
   - Autoscaler saturation + queue growth > 500rps backlog

Decision matrix (signal => action):
- Safety-critical behavioral: immediate full traffic cutover to fallback model variant + notify on-call + create post-mortem stub. Automation: YES (unconditional). Human override: allowed but requires senior steward ack.
- Business-impact: traffic throttling to safe baseline slice (e.g., 50% of experiment traffic), degrade to cached responses where applicable. Automation: YES (conditional — require confirmation from rollout steward for first trigger in a given day).
- Performance: graceful degradation (reduce max tokens, switch to lower-latency quantized model) and increase batching thresholds. Automation: YES (tunable cooldown).
- Infrastructure: increase capacity or reroute traffic to other regions; if capacity unavailable, divert to hosted safe model; escalate to SRE. Automation: partial.

Automation contract (fields every automation rule must include):
- rule_id: human-friendly short id (e.g., AF-01-safety-cut)
- triggers: list of signals (as above) with aggregation window and threshold
- action: canonical action type (cut-to-fallback, throttle, degrade, reroute, scale-up)
- prechecks: quick sanity checks before action (e.g., ensure fallback variant health >= 95%)
- cooldown: seconds/minutes before the same rule can fire again
- audit: required metadata written to experiment ledger (timestamp, triggering signal, prechecks result, actor=automation/human id)
- rollback: how to revert action, who can revert automatically vs manually

Example rule (human-readable):
- AF-01-safety-cut:
  triggers: policy_violation_rate > 0.002 over 3m
  action: cut-to-fallback (0% experiment, 100% baseline)
  prechecks: fallback_model_healthy == true
  cooldown: 30m
  audit: write to rollout_log and notify #release-ops
  rollback: automatic rollback after 60m if metric back to baseline for 10m, else manual.

ChatOps integration (principles):
- Single canonical channel: #release-ops for signals, #oncall for urgent pages.
- All automation actions emit a standardized message with action_id, rule_id, and one-click actions (confirm/abort/revert).
- ChatOps commands must be idempotent and require role checks (who can execute what).

Suggested ChatOps command set (examples to implement in bot):
- /rollout status <experiment-id>  => shows current traffic split, active rules, last triggered events\- /rollout pause <experiment-id>  => holds new activations; idempotent\- /rollout cut-to-fallback <experiment-id> --rule AF-01  => triggers AF-01 if prechecks pass (bot returns precheck summary)
- /rollout throttle <experiment-id> --percent 50 --reason "latency" => throttles experiment traffic to percent\- /rollout revert <experiment-id> --to="previous" --confirm => reverts latest automation action (requires 2 approvers if action was auto-triggered)
- /rollout resume <experiment-id> => resumes normal experiment traffic after human review

ChatOps message templates (bot -> channel):
- Automation-fired template:
  [AUTOMATION] rule_id=AF-01-safety-cut experiment=exp-2026-03-14 trigger=policy_violation_rate=0.003 window=3m action=cut-to-fallback status=success audit_id=RAL-974
- Human-action template:
  [MANUAL] actor=Priya Nair action=throttle experiment=exp-2026-03-14 details="50% throttle due to p95 latency"

Escalation choreography (30/60/120 min tiers):
- 0-30m: automation containment; immediate notify steering channel and on-call. Owner: rollout steward.
- 30-60m: if metric not recovered, SRE and product manager paged. Initial incident stub created and triage call scheduled. Owner: SRE lead.
- 60-120m: executive notification if user-visible degradation continues or revenue impact estimated > threshold. Owner: PM and Eng manager.

Observability and post-incident artifacts:
- Required artifacts for any automated fallback event:
  - snapshot of signal timelines (15m pre, 60m post)
  - affected cohort definitions and synthetic test runs
  - automation audit log entry and raw precheck outputs
  - ChatOps transcript of actions and approvals
- Postmortem template must include: timeline, root cause hypothesis, automation rule evaluation (did it help/harm?), recommended rule changes, and follow-up owners.

Safety caveats and gotchas (lessons from field trials):
- False positives from synthetic traffic can trip automated safety rules; sanitize telemetry to exclude synthetic cohorts before evaluating rules.
- Cascading fallbacks may hide root cause; prefer single-step fallbacks and hold complex multi-step automation behind additional confirmations.
- Telemetry lag matters: ensure metric windows account for ingestion latency to avoid oscillation.

Next steps and open questions (working items):
- Implement AF-01 and AF-03 in staging and run chaos scenarios (responsible: Jonah).
- Build ChatOps bot handlers for /rollout cut-to-fallback and /rollout status (responsible: Eng-Devex).
- Define role matrix for who can confirm automated actions (SRE, steward, PM) and implement RBAC in ChatOps (responsible: Security).
- Draft short training for stewards and on-call on interpreting automation prechecks and manual overrides.

Appendix: quick checklist for stewards when a rule fires
1) Read automation precheck summary (health, perf, fallback readiness).
2) Verify user-facing impact (sample session logs / repro).
3) Decide: let automation continue, throttle further, or escalate to manual reversion.
4) Document decision in ChatOps and attach incident stub.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Consider an "observe-only" mode for rules during first 48h of deployment.
- Explore tagging experiment cohorts so automation can be cohort-aware.
- Audit: persist automation decisions in the platform's rollout ledger with signed actors.

End of draft.
